study: Buy-stop entries filtered by buyer-initiated order flow, at the desk's actual cost (operator 2026-10-24): the two real-but-small effects found so far combined - (1) a buy-stop through the oversold minute's high (batch 2 T2: +2.0 / +2.4 bp vs random, t 5-10, gross +1.9 / +2.8 bp) and (2) Lee-Ready buyer-initiated SIP trade flow in the 60 s before the decision (order_flow_pilot G1: +1.5-2 bp, t ~3.5). Does a buy-stop whose trigger arrives on strong buy flow make money after paying the quoted spread?
registered_at: 2026-10-24, before any tick fetch or outcome for this study
prior: LOW-MEDIUM (~15%): two independent ~2 bp effects; if additive and the flow filter does not merely select names that already moved, a G1-IN buy-stop could reach ~+3-4 bp gross, close to the desk's ~3 bp round trip on $20+ names. Risks: the effects overlap (both measure buying pressure at the turn), and quoted spreads at a stop trigger are wider than average.
population: Batch 2 T2 trades (tools/studies/batch2.py, sha as scored 2026-10-24) on the warehouse, sessions 2026-05-11 .. 10-15, ENTRY PRICE >= $20 (the desk's floor). Halves A <= 07-29 < B. The T2 rule, stop level, fill minute k and exit minute are unchanged (IEX lines, SIP trigger).
sample: A seeded random sample of the population (seed 'bsf-sample'), stratified by day (equal share per day), size set by the budget probe: the largest N (<= 8,000 per half) whose estimated fetch time is <= 6 hours at <= 150 requests/min on the data-only account. Selection never reads outcomes.
trigger_time: T = the timestamp of the first SIP trade (pilot KEEP_CODES) inside fill minute k with price >= stop + $0.01; a trade whose trigger cannot be found in the trade tape is dropped (counted).
flow: OFI60 exactly as order_flow_pilot.features: Lee-Ready signed SIP volume share over [T - 60 s, T) (quotes <= 60 s old for signing, tick test at the mid, >= 5 signed trades, else missing). G1 side: IN = top tercile by (OFI60, tie_u) with the cut set on HALF A only (order_flow_pilot.top_cut / groups, tie_u seeded on sym|day|minute); OUT = the rest with the feature; missing = excluded (counted, reported by side).
actual_cost: QUOTED round trip (the desk fills at the touch): entry = the ASK of the last clean SIP quote at or before T + 1 s (<= 30 s old); exit = the BID of the last clean quote at or before the exit time + 1 s (<= 30 s old), where the exit time is the start of the T2 exit fill minute (u+1) or 15:59:59 for an end-of-day exit. NET = exit bid / entry ask - 1. No other cost (paper has no commission). A trade lacking either quote is dropped (counted by side).
primary: G1-IN trades: per half, per day the mean NET; day-equal; day-clustered t.
pass: In BOTH halves: G1-IN mean NET > 0 with t >= 2.0, AND (G1-IN minus G1-OUT day-mean NET) >= 0 (point estimate; the flow filter must add), AND dropping the 3 best days and (separately) the top 5 names keeps G1-IN NET >= 0.
fail: G1-IN NET t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound of G1-IN NET < 0 in both halves. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED.
power: Outcome-blind count step after the tick fetch: G1-IN / OUT / missing trades and days per half; MDE = (2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day mean of the sampled trades' same-name random-entry control returns from the batch2 rows - control returns only, never the trades') / sqrt(days of G1-IN) <= 3 bp; floors >= 300 G1-IN trades and >= 20 days per half; --score refuses otherwise.
fetch: Data-only Alpaca account (secrets_data.json), after hours, paced <= 150 requests/min: per sampled trade (a) SIP trades over [k_start - 60 s, k_end] (finds T and the flow window), (b) SIP quotes over [T - 120 s, T + 1 s], (c) SIP quotes over [exit - 30 s, exit + 1 s]. C4: 429s retried; any unrecovered failure, truncated page or missing file refuses scoring; failures and drops counted.
information_only: G1-OUT NET and the whole sample's NET (the unfiltered buy-stop at quoted cost)
IN minus OUT on bar-based gross (separates the flow effect from spread differences)
the quoted spread at entry and exit by side (is the spread at a stop trigger wider than average?)
G2 (quote imbalance at T) and G3 (G1 and G2) sides
the batch2 bar-based gross of the same sampled trades vs the quoted NET (the cost decomposition)
confirmation: A PASS is re-run unchanged on warehouse_confirm (2026-01-14 .. 04-24, never read; its T2 trades computed with the same code, ticks fetched only then), then a forward paper prereg; never a desk change by itself.
multiplicity: One primary. Declared family context: this combines two effects found in earlier tests (batch 2, order_flow_pilot); a single-test t >= 2 is the bar, and a PASS is labelled 'combination of earlier findings' until confirmed.
declared_deviations: SIP ticks and quotes (the live desk sees IEX quotes/trades; a live version would need the desk to compute flow on its own feed or buy SIP)
the stop LEVEL is set from IEX bars and TRIGGERED by SIP prints (as batch 2 T2)
buy-stop fills modelled at the quoted ask at the trigger, not at the stop price
no_retuning: $20 floor, 60 s flow window, top-tercile cut from half A, quote ages, exit rule, halves, floors and the bar are fixed.

amended.when: 2026-10-24, operator ('can we leverage this knowing our exits will help'), before the skeptic review and before any fetch.
changes: TWO ARMS, co-primary. ARM A = the registered rule (T2 %R turn-down exit, quoted NET). ARM B = the SAME G1-IN entries exited by the desk's LIVE exit stack: tools/studies/exit_capture.walk at zero drift (leash_replay walk, plan stop, ratchet/leash, trail-exit trend hold on IEX 1-minute bars, dead_trade, 15:50 end) under the live config of each trade's day as exit_capture loads it. Entry = the quoted ask at T + 1 s; exit = exit_capture.exit_price (min(trigger, bid) for stop exits, the bid otherwise). RISK (R) = entry x the MEDIAN risk/entry ratio of the desk's real fills in the exit_capture cache (2026-09-23 .. 10-20), because the desk's exit knobs are set in R and percent and a synthetic entry has no desk-sized R; the plan stop = entry - R.

ARM B data: SIP trades from T to min(T + walk MAX_HOLD, 15:50) for G1-IN sampled trades only (exit_capture's second rows), bids as exit_capture.fetch_bid; the joint fetch (A + B) obeys the 6-hour budget rule (N reduced until it fits).

PASS (study) if EITHER arm meets its pass conditions with t >= 2.24 in both halves (Bonferroni over 2 arms) instead of 2.0; the (IN - OUT) and drop conditions apply to arm A only (arm B has no OUT side); arm B adds drop-3-days and drop-5-names >= 0. Both arms are always reported. FAIL per arm as registered; the study FAILS if both arms fail.

Declared prior for arm B: the 10/21 exit study found the live exits keep ~70-78% of a fast 3-minute edge and need ~+11 bp of entry edge to break even on the desk's fills; with a ~2-4 bp entry edge arm B is expected to lose, unless the buy-stop's edge arrives fast and the leash keeps it.

changes: (0) DECLARED: both ingredients were chosen as winners on these same 110 sessions (T2 best of 7 batch-2 tests; G1 best of 3 pilot groups). Only the flow-on-T2 interaction and the quoted cost are new; any PASS is a re-read of known effects until it repeats on warehouse_confirm.

(1) T = the first ROUND-LOT print (conditions subset of {' ', '@', 'F'}; odd lots 'I' and Z/U/T excluded, as leash_replay.fetch_seconds) in fill minute k with price >= stop + $0.01. The OFI60 flow feature keeps the pilot's definition (odd lots included).

(2) ENTRY = max(the ask of the last clean quote in [T - 3 s, T + 1 s], the trigger print's price); a missing quote in that window drops the trade (counted by side); the share with ask < trigger is reported. Information: entry at the ask at T + 3 s and T + 11 s (the desk's median arm-to-fill is 11 s).

(3) ARM B CONFIG: one config, the current config/bot_config.json, sha256 prefix 837dfd79268ebf16 (the live config after the operator's 10/23 16:10 change); the run refuses another sha. There is no per-day historical exit config.

(4) ARM B R = entry x 0.05009 (the median risk/entry of 1,177 desk 'watch' fills >= $20 in ai_reports/outcomes.jsonl; p25 0.04981, p75 0.05041); spread_r = the SIP quoted spread at the entry quote / R.

(5) ARM B PATHS: SIP prints fetched in chunks (T .. T + 15 min, then + 45 min, then to min(T + 120 min, 15:50)) and the walk re-run on each extension; an exit counts only if it falls before the fetched end (else extend). Budget: time-based (seconds per trade measured by the probe, the SDK pages internally), the joint A + B fetch must fit 6 hours; 429s retried.

(6) POWER: MDE = (2.24 + 0.84) x SD(day means of G1-IN trades' same-name control returns) / sqrt(days) <= 3 bp. PROJECTED before the fetch from the batch2 control rows (outcome-blind): N = 8,000 per half (G1-IN ~48/day) gives 2.63 / 2.23 bp; N = 4,000 gives 3.70 / 3.05 bp. So N = 8,000 per half (if the budget allows; otherwise UNDERPOWERED is declared before fetching). Realistic best case declared: T2 gross ~2-3 bp + flow ~1.5 bp - quoted cost ~3+ bp = ~0-1 bp net.
(7) FAIL per arm: t <= -2 in a half, or the 98.75% upper bound (Bonferroni over 2 arms) of the arm's NET < 0 in both halves.
(8) POPULATION pinned: batch2 rows.json as scored 2026-10-24 (module_sha256 recorded in the sample file); the $20 floor applies to the batch fill price px = max(stop, SIP open of k).

(9) CONFIRMATION reuses half A's numeric OFI60 cut and R = 0.05009 (no re-cut on the confirmation window). Declared: 15+ preregs name the same 70-session window as their confirmation; each use erodes it.
(minor) (IN - OUT) is reported with its t; SPY-hedged NET (minus SPY's SIP return over the same entry-exit minutes) and drop rates for missing T / quotes by side are information.
